title: OSHA general industry materials handling and storage practice questions
description: Free OSHA materials handling practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart N: storage, rim wheels, cranes, crane inspections and slings, each linked to its source.

questions.question: Under 1910.176(c), storage areas must be kept free from accumulations of materials that constitute which hazards?

options.A: Noise only
options.B: Tripping, fire, explosion, or pest harborage
options.C: Glare and reflections
options.D: Electrical interference with radios

questions.explanation: 1910.176(c) states: "Storage areas shall be kept free from accumulation of materials that constitute hazards from tripping, fire, explosion, or pest harborage."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.176, Handling materials—general (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A rolling railroad car on a spur track could enter a building or a work area. What does 1910.176(f) require on that spur track?

options.A: A flagger posted at the building door
options.B: Wheel chocks on each car only
options.C: A warning bell at the track switch
options.D: Derail and/or bumper blocks

questions.explanation: 1910.176(f) states that "Derail and/or bumper blocks shall be provided on spur railroad tracks where a rolling car could contact other cars being worked, enter a building, work or traffic area."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.176, Handling materials—general (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: 1910.177 covers rim wheels used on large vehicles such as trucks, buses and off-road machines. Which rim wheel servicing does its scope paragraph exclude?

options.A: Rim wheels used on automobiles
options.B: Rim wheels used on buses
options.C: Rim wheels used on off-road machines
options.D: Single piece rim wheels used on trailers

questions.explanation: The section applies to rim wheels "used on large vehicles such as trucks, tractors, trailers, buses and off-road machines" and "does not apply to the servicing of rim wheels used on automobiles."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.177, Servicing multi-piece and single piece rim wheels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.177(d)(3)(i), each restraining device or barrier must withstand the maximum force transferred to it during a rim wheel separation at a set pressure. What pressure does the rule set?

options.A: 100 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure
options.B: 110 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure
options.C: 150 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure
options.D: 125 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure

questions.explanation: Each restraining device or barrier must withstand the force of "a rim wheel separation occurring at 150 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure for the type of rim wheel being serviced."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.177, Servicing multi-piece and single piece rim wheels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1910.177(d)(3)(iii) require restraining devices and barriers to be visually inspected?

options.A: Prior to each day's use and after any separation or sudden release of contained air
options.B: Once a week and after any separation of the rim wheel components
options.C: Once a month, with a written record
options.D: Only after a rim wheel separation has occurred

questions.explanation: Restraining devices and barriers "shall be visually inspected prior to each day's use and after any separation of the rim wheel components or sudden release of contained air."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.177, Servicing multi-piece and single piece rim wheels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A rim wheel restraining device needs rewelding. Under 1910.177(d)(3)(iv), who must certify it as meeting the strength requirements before it returns to service?

options.A: The tire technician who last used it
options.B: Either the manufacturer or a Registered Professional Engineer
options.C: Any shop supervisor
options.D: The local fire marshal

questions.explanation: Restraining devices or barriers needing structural repair such as component replacement or rewelding "shall not be returned to service until they are certified by either the manufacturer or a Registered Professional Engineer as meeting the strength requirements of paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.177, Servicing multi-piece and single piece rim wheels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where must the rated load of an overhead or gantry crane be marked under 1910.179(b)(5)?

options.A: Only in the operator's manual kept in the office
options.B: On the runway rail next to the end stop
options.C: On a sign at the building entrance
options.D: Plainly on each side of the crane

questions.explanation: 1910.179(b)(5) states that "The rated load of the crane shall be plainly marked on each side of the crane." Each hoist of a crane with more than one hoisting unit is also marked, legible from the ground or floor.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An overhead crane is to be modified and rerated. Under 1910.179(b)(3), who must check the modifications and the supporting structure for the new rated load?

options.A: The crane operator
options.B: An OSHA compliance officer
options.C: A qualified engineer or the equipment manufacturer
options.D: The building's insurance carrier

questions.explanation: Cranes may be modified and rerated "provided such modifications and the supporting structure are checked thoroughly for the new rated load by a qualified engineer or the equipment manufacturer." The crane is then tested under paragraph (k)(2).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1910.179(n)(4)(i) require the upper limit switch of each hoist to be tried out under no load?

options.A: Once a month
options.B: Only during the annual periodic inspection
options.C: Only after a rated load test
options.D: At the beginning of each operator's shift

questions.explanation: "At the beginning of each operator's shift, the upper limit switch of each hoist shall be tried out under no load." If the switch does not operate properly, the appointed person is notified immediately.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.179(j)(1)(ii) define the interval for periodic inspection of overhead and gantry cranes in regular service?

options.A: 1 to 12-month intervals
options.B: Every 18 months
options.C: Every 2 to 5 years
options.D: Once every 3 years

questions.explanation: The rule designates two classifications: "Frequent inspection—Daily to monthly intervals" and "Periodic inspection—1 to 12-month intervals."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Prior to initial use, which overhead and gantry cranes does 1910.179(k)(1)(i) require to be tested?

options.A: Only cranes rated over 10 tons
options.B: Only cranes bought used
options.C: All new and altered cranes
options.D: Only cranes installed outdoors

questions.explanation: "Prior to initial use all new and altered cranes shall be tested to insure compliance with this section", including hoisting and lowering, trolley travel, bridge travel, and limit switches, locking and safety devices.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A crane's rope has been idle for a month or more because the crane was shut down. What does 1910.179(m)(2) require before the rope is used?

options.A: Lubrication only
options.B: A thorough inspection for all types of deterioration by an appointed person, whose approval is required for further use
options.C: Replacement of the rope in every case
options.D: Nothing, if the rope was inspected before the shutdown

questions.explanation: Such rope "shall be given a thorough inspection before it is used. This inspection shall be for all types of deterioration and shall be performed by an appointed person whose approval shall be required for further use of the rope."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For crawler, locomotive and truck cranes, what upper limit does 1910.180(e)(2)(ii) set for rated load test loads?

options.A: 125 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius
options.B: 150 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius
options.C: 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius
options.D: 200 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius

questions.explanation: 1910.180(e)(2)(ii) states: "Test loads shall not exceed 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.180, Crawler locomotive and truck cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where does 1910.180(c)(2) require the load rating chart of a crawler, locomotive or truck crane to be fixed?

options.A: To the crane cab, easily visible to the operator while seated at the control station
options.B: In the employer's main office files
options.C: On a board at the entrance to the work area
options.D: Inside the toolbox stored on the crane

questions.explanation: The rating chart must be "securely fixed to the crane cab in a location easily visible to the operator while seated at his control station."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.180, Crawler locomotive and truck cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.184(c)(5) require for slings used in a basket hitch?

options.A: That only nylon web slings be used
options.B: That they be loaded at double their rated capacity
options.C: That they be shortened with a knot to fit the load
options.D: That the loads be balanced to prevent slippage

questions.explanation: 1910.184(c)(5) states: "Slings used in a basket hitch shall have the loads balanced to prevent slippage."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.184(c)(14) state about slings without affixed and legible identification markings?

options.A: They may be used at half their rated capacity
options.B: Employers must not use them
options.C: They may be used for up to 30 days
options.D: They may be used if the operator approves

questions.explanation: 1910.184(c)(14) states: "Employers must not use slings without affixed and legible identification markings."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.184(c)(11) state about shock loading of slings?

options.A: Shock loading is prohibited
options.B: It is allowed up to the sling's rated capacity
options.C: It is allowed with a basket hitch only
options.D: It is allowed once a competent person approves it

questions.explanation: Among the safe operating practices that apply whenever any sling is used, 1910.184(c)(11) states: "Shock loading is prohibited."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which condition does 1910.184(g)(9) list for immediately removing a metal mesh sling from service?

options.A: Use at a temperature of 100 degrees F
options.B: A durable marking stating the rated capacity
options.C: A broken weld or broken brazed joint along the sling edge
options.D: Handles with a rated capacity equal to the metal fabric

questions.explanation: Metal mesh slings "shall be immediately removed from service" for listed conditions, including "A broken weld or broken brazed joint along the sling edge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must the permanently affixed durable identification on an alloy steel chain sling state under 1910.184(e)(1)?

options.A: The purchase date and price
options.B: The owner's name only
options.C: The color code and the chain's weight
options.D: Size, grade, rated capacity, and reach

questions.explanation: 1910.184(e)(1) states: "Alloy steel chain slings shall have permanently affixed durable identification stating size, grade, rated capacity, and reach."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.184(i)(6)(i), nylon web slings must not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of which substances are present?

options.A: Caustics
options.B: Acids or phenolics
options.C: Water or steam
options.D: Oils or greases

questions.explanation: 1910.184(i)(6)(i) states: "Nylon web slings shall not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of acids or phenolics are present." The caustics limit in (i)(6)(ii) is for polyester and polypropylene web slings.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)
